note: The expectation is COMPUTED, not written down. This case was pinned at 201, itself a re-baseline from 194, and failed on 2026-09-08 because the true answer had become 206: calibrationDueOn dates pass as real time advances, so five more sensors fell overdue and the system reported them correctly. A frozen number for a quantity that moves with the calendar is a scheduled false alarm — it decays quietly and fires on a day nobody chose. Weakening it to 'contains a number' would kill the noise and the point together; the point is to catch a WRONG figure.
expect_sparql: PREFIX ontosage: <http://ontosage.org/capabilities#> PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?s) AS ?n) WHERE { ?s ontosage:calibrationDueOn ?due . FILTER(xsd:date(?due) < xsd:date(NOW())) }

note: WB-04..22 (2026-09-15): a building-wide ranking is answered within the row budget, naming its coverage. It used to assert the decline; the decline is now wrong for this building size. BUG-599: a room with an unmeasured criterion must not rank first.
why: The deliberation lane compiles a CQ-IR, enumerates candidate spaces, fetches every modality for each and scores them. Measured solo on 2026-09-11: 37.7 s for the over-budget decline and 22.9 s for the Floor 3 ranking — but BOTH exceeded the probe's 120 s default during a full run, while the same run finished 59 cases in 21.9 min. The lane is legitimately slow and gets slower under load. 300 s is a stated per-case allowance, which is the probe's own sanctioned pattern: raising the DEFAULT would hide a genuine hang, so the allowance sits on the case that needs it. This does not weaken the assertion — a wrong answer still fails; it stops a known-slow lane failing for being slow. See CAVEAT-500.

question: Is the lift working?
why: Protects against a declared asset reported as absent - the pre-W0 answer was 'This building has no lifts recorded in its model' about a lift the building describes in a published accessibility survey (BUG-438). CORRECTED 2026-09-10: this case briefly also forbade 'of 1 lift', on the reading that '1 of 1 lift(s)' was a denominator over the retrieved set. That was wrong. asset_state_service._status_query asks '?asset a ontosage:Lift' and exactly one subject carries that type, so the count is correct for what the lane asks. The real defect is that three brick:Elevator are declared elsewhere and the lane never sees them (BUG-497) - which no marker over this answer can currently detect, because the honest answer does not exist yet. When it does, assert that the count DISCLOSES its basis.

question: How many sensors are there in total?
why: Two failures, neither assertable as a bare number. (a) 'Floors: 8' stated flat in a six-storey building - the figure is right and the reading is wrong, so the marker is the EXPLANATION. question: How many floors does this building have?
expect_sparql: PREFIX brick: <https://brickschema.org/schema/Brick#> SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?f) AS ?n) WHERE { ?f a brick:Floor }
why: Building-agnostic. The figure is computed from whichever graph is live, so the case is true of any building and rots for none. A literal here would make it bldg1-only and would decay the first time a floor was added - the failure TODO-484 records, where a pinned overdue-calibration count went 194 -> 201 -> 206 while the system stayed right.
